title: Is it valid to use ai to make my game ideas come to life?
author: echukun
selftext:
I am trying to be a game designer and I have been trying for a while, after working on a few projects Im starting to realize this is a time consuming and long task as fun as it is.  
I do not have a Dev or coding background. I completed a Bachelors in Design so I could find a way into the Video game Industry.  
I have 2 projects which have a good amount of contribution from me.  
MY MAIN REASON TO POST THIS BEING.  
I HAVE SOME REALLY GREAT IDEAS FOR GAMES but when i begin working on them the artwork and the scope always end up discouraging me. I have the vision for it but not the skill or maybe the patience to sit and work on each part of the project on my own.  
I've learned godot and added the ziva plugin so I can have the AI help me

comments.author: Living_Cell7304
comments.body: What a useless post. Go try it. Either it works or it doesn’t.

comments.author: thirsty_pretzelzz
comments.body:
Yes! 

These tools allow any ordinary but dedicated Individual to build the game they’ve always dreamt of (within reason) Will anyone play it? Who knows, tbh most games made don’t make a profit but make it for you first and foremost, enjoy the journey and if others love playing it too then that’s a bonus

comments.author: raygarraty47
comments.body: So what exactly is your question? Is it worth doing it with ai? Why not, but if you throw big scope project into any AI, result will be trash. It will take a lot of time to do so ething if quality, regardless if you use ai or not

comments.author: c235k
comments.body: A bachelors in design and you don’t have the skill or patience? Sounds like you set yourself up for failure

comments.author: TechgeekOne
comments.body: Designers aren't generally expected to do that stuff. So why would it be a problem? You'd work with engineers and artists to build the game anyway in a studio. The only differences is in this case it's an AI instead of humans.

comments.author: LegoFighter2
comments.body: Creating games is craftsmanship. That mean, you  have to do it, learn it, redo it for years. No offense, but you seem to be impatient and hasty.

replies.author: oSi7ENT
replies.body: This. I’m working on my first game. Made some headway and realized I had been ordering AI to do bandaid coding… So I then went back and spent nearly a week getting to code in real dynamic systems that run in conjunction based on math. The results have been amazing and I’m still on part 1 of the project.

comments.author: lordpoee
comments.body: Start small, simple, then grow. Don't try to make a great big game in one shot if you are new to AI development. Start small, learn how to prompt, learn game development terminology and how it applies.GDD is your friend- Game Development Document. Always roadmap for larger projects. Do the GDD then roadmap it. Make the mechanical demo first THEN make it pretty.

comments.author: tonios2
comments.body: God help me, I have ideas, but im too lazy to do anything

comments.author: GlobalCurry
comments.body: Just try it out, the best advice is to work on project management skills and breaking down tasks. AI can do that a bit but it's one of those things humans still do better in practice. The smaller and more precise a task you give the AI, the better the outcome will be.

comments.author: SigmaANenigma
comments.body:
If you're willing to engage and ruffle some feathers. If your willing to face targeted persecution(a wave that will wash over in 10 years when the Overton window (acceptable consensus to the public) shifts. And if AI generated/assisted work becomes socially acceptable; you don't want to be caught off with your pants on the floor then- YES!  Get into it right away. Don't ponder about it and don't be guilt tripped about it. The largest negative is that the bar is going to be raised. The people who will be doing code manually, will either be  curation engineers, serious ai infrastructure developers or they will be jobless. 

The best and worst thing about ai game dev is that bar is raised. You have to make something good now to win. And here's a another thing if you want to survive you'll have to focus on curating a personal audience much the same way big companies do. It's the only way to survive the wave. But at least the average person is dumbing down that's a huge advantage to analytical thinkers.

A lot of people will be cloning without two thoughts. Some might try and one shot a game. They can't buy taste, they can't buy scope, they might not even be able to fix bugs with...the llm.


 So gitgud and early too.

comments.author: goektasgaming
comments.body:
I do that all the time. I am not good in describing my ideas exactly but the AI can describe your idea into a concept. You read it and figure out if it understood your idea. If not, iterate.  
Here is my Workflow:  
I get an idea! -> AI, do a first concept draft -> iterate draft until i am satisfied -> AI, do a design draft -> iterate draft until i am satisfied -> first MVP prototype -> iterate so many times until i think it's good -> first real feature, like the first level idea. Repeat that 200-1000 times and you get something that is not Slop anymore. And always involve friends and family for testing and feedback first before asking strangers. Strangers on the internet expect something at least good.

comments.author: BadgerPast4204
comments.body: Si, estás solo, normalmente un juego se hace mínimo entre 3 personas, hablo de vn ya no hablemos de algo mínimamente complejo

comments.author: AccomplishedIce8766
comments.body: You can try learning coding, and one day you'll succeed

comments.author: Disastrous-Round-150
comments.body:
Do as I do! 100% from scratch and 100% procedural, zero game engines and zero game assets. It sounds like more work but it's quite the opposite. I can turn a well thought through game idea into a working game prototype within 1 hour with GPT 6 Astra set at max in work mode.

This way I can focus on game mechanics and game play what really matters in a game, without having to think of making game assets and game engines. Assets and engines waste a lot of toll usage time with back and forth with the AI.

It's better to have a full working game prototype with the game mechanics and game play dialed in before going to the step of making game assets and choosing a game engine which you see fit for your game. Or you can simply stay 100% procedural the procedural capabilities of current AIs are astonishing and without a game engine you are 100% in charge of what is happening underneath.

comments.author: lorekeeper32
comments.body: Its easier than ever these days. I gave up adobe software and blender years ago. I was in a rut and couldnt handle the workload of my own passion projects with life. But with ai, i just lay down in bed and prompt away now. It literally does everything. Its alien technology atp. Ive launched several games now. Im working on 4 games currently right now. 2 weeks ago it was 6. Are they ai slop? Yes, but they are decent. I know it.
